$comment: Relation schema. The single source of truth for which relation may connect which pair of node kinds. docs/RELATIONS.md is generated from this file's intent and must not disagree with it; scripts/audit.mjs should validate against this table, not against a list inside the audit. Status: PROPOSAL, not yet enforced.
$principle: A node's `kind` decides which relations may leave it. This is the standard the two-relation scheme never had: `children` currently means contains, breaks-down-into, is-made-by, belongs-to-the-same-organisation-as, and is-a-note-about.

directions.$comment: Three different directions, previously conflated into one sentence in RELATIONS.md §3. Confusing them is how the viewer ended up drawing a supply chain as a nested tree.
directions.storage: Which node holds the edge in the data file. Always the container or the consumer.
directions.upstream: The direction a reader walks to get back toward the mine. This is what reachability is defined on (RELATIONS.md §8).
directions.arrow: What the viewer draws. Refinement edges point outward from the object; flow edges point along the direction of physical movement.

connectivity.$comment: Which relations admit a node into the graph (RELATIONS.md §8). Separate from `family`, which is about how the edge is DRAWN. A relation can be drawn as a cross-link and still count for membership.
connectivity.uses_note: DECIDED 2026-10-04: `uses` DOES carry connectivity, downward from a reached process. A stamping press had to be built, so admitting it is correct. Measured cost: zero. The 195 tool nodes it admits are already reachable by the generic downward walk on today's edges, because process->tool is currently a `children` edge. The decision only starts to bite once `uses` is separated from `contains` -- at which point it admits those 195 nodes for the right reason rather than by accident. Revisitable.

narrow_kinds.$comment: Relations where the target kind is deliberately restricted. Kept explicit because the first draft allowed `consumes -> part` by accident. NOTE: these are ASSERTIONS checked after classification, never a router -- an early version of relate.mjs used them to route edges and mis-bucketed all 126 `*->part` edges as judgements.
narrow_kinds.consumes_part: NOT ALLOWED. DECIDED 2026-10-04: a process does not take in discrete objects. It melts, dissolves and reacts substances; the objects in its shop are its equipment (`uses`) or its products (`produces`). Zero edges in the current tree need this, so removing it costs nothing and removes an ambiguity an agent would otherwise have to resolve. CONSEQUENCE: `process->part`, `tool->part` and `facility->part` are all MECHANICAL, not judgements.
narrow_kinds.produces_part: ALLOWED. DECIDED 2026-10-04: moulding yields the case, wave soldering yields the soldered board, die attach yields the bonded die. 89 edges.

kinds.$comment: Proposed additions to SCHEMA.md's kind list. `org` and `site` split the overloaded `facility`; utilities become `material`.

added.org: A company or other legal entity. Distinct from a place: Commodore Business Machines (UK) Ltd is an org; Corby is a site. Exists so that `owned by` is a table lookup rather than an edge judgement.
added.site: A place that is not a production facility: a cleanroom bay, an amber room, a pipeline, a harbour.

retyped.$comment: Verified counts from the built tree, 2026-10-04.
retyped.facility -> org: at least 17, including bare company names currently filed as sites: Signetics, Motorola, Fairchild, Texas Instruments, National Semiconductor, Kentron, CE(HK)L, CBM Santa Clara
retyped.facility -> site: the rooms, bays, networks and stacks: cleanroom bays, litho area, ring main, LNG terminal, pipeline
retyped.facility -> material: 5 utility deliveries still typed facility: facility.electricity (177 in-edges), facility.water (47), facility.steam (6), facility.gases (4), facility.compressed-air (2). facility.nitrogen AND facility.helium are ALREADY kind material, so the tree is currently inconsistent with itself here -- two utilities were typed one way and five the other. Verified: these five are every facility that is the target of a `from` edge.

content_defects_found.$comment: Not kind errors -- these are wrong nodes or wrong edges, found while checking the retyping table.
content_defects_found.product_index_typed_as_material: metal.copper is named 'Copper: track, winding wire, foil, contacts' and is the target of 52 from-edges. It is a PRODUCT INDEX, not a substance: `made of metal.copper -> metal.copper.wire` is circular. Probably wants splitting into a substance node plus a grouping node. That is a content change, own pass.
content_defects_found.compound_where_a_stream_was_meant: c64.case.shield.foil has inputs ['metal.aluminum.ingot', 'c64.packaging.kraft-pulp']. The prose says 'foil carried on a cardboard backing', so the intended target is the backing LAMINATE; kraft pulp is what the backing is made from. Under the spec-sheet test this is `made from`, not `made of`.
content_defects_found.ingredient_rows_naming_products: 63 of 155 curated rows in _ingredients.json give a string absent from the target's name. Nine point at a process, three at a facility, one at a tool -- none of which any table permits as a `made of` target. Review all 63 before the mechanical pass leans on this table.

contains.test: Could you point at it inside the other thing?
contains.note: A machine contains its machines: Steam turbine -> Surface condenser, Generator, GSU. All 30 of today's tool->tool edges are this and were being mis-filed as site structure.

made of.test: Would a spec sheet for the parent list the target as a component? The target keeps its own chemical identity: a mixture, alloy, blend or formulation. Equivalently: is the parent the SAME substance as the target in a different shape?
made of.note: CALIBRATION WARNING (agent B). This relation's stored list permits `part->material`, but the `part->material` judgement question offers only `contains | made of`. The mechanical pass and the judgement pass could therefore produce DIFFERENT relations for the same kind-pair. Fixed by _judgement_overrides_mechanical below.
examples: metal.solder -> refined tin, refined lead -- a solder spec lists Sn 63 / Pb 37
metal.solder -> antimony addition -- still antimony in the alloy
chem.solder-chemicals.rosin-flux -> pine rosin -- a flux spec lists rosin, activator, solvent
metal.ferrite -> metal.ferrite.bead -- the bead's spec is NiZn or MnZn ferrite

made from.arrow: from the mine toward the object
made from.test: The input is transformed: reacted, reduced, melted into a network, alloyed, or separated. The target does NOT appear on the parent's spec sheet.
examples: chem.glass-fiber -> borax -- THE decisive case. Borax decomposes to Na2O + B2O3 + water; the boron survives as B2O3 in the network, the borax does not. An E-glass spec sheet reads SiO2, B2O3, CaO, Na2O.
metal.silica.polysilicon -> metal.silica.tcs -- the rod is Si 9N; no TCS survives
metal.silica.mgsi -> metal.quartzite -- reduced with coke; the Si survives, the oxygen and carbon do not
metal.silica.tcs -> metal.silica.mgsi -- chlorinated at 300 C; the Si survives, the chlorine does not
chem.glass-fiber.borax -> colemanite ore -- Na2B4O7.10H2O is the product; the ore is not a component
facility.steam.ion-resin -> styrene monomer -- crosslinked PS-DVB is not styrene
metal.steel -> metal.coke, metal.limestone -- both consumed into the melt
facility.power.uranium-ore -> uranium fuel -- refined, enriched, fabricated
made from.guard: SHORTCUT, DELIBERATELY REDUNDANT. DECIDED 2026-10-04: KEPT, even where a process route exists. A material's direct feedstock is what a reader wants when they ask 'what is this made of', and the shortcut is one click where the route is four. The redundancy is the feature. What is unacceptable is the two copies DISAGREEING, so the audit checks agreement rather than mere existence.
made from.audit: A `made from` edge paralleling an existing (produces -> consumes) route is a WARN, not a FAIL: both are listed for a human to compare. A FAIL only if the shortcut names a substance the route contradicts.

made by.note: NOT STORED. Derived at build time as: the set of processes that `produce` me. Storing it would duplicate `produces` (point 3 of docs/assessment.md). The viewer renders the derived set as the expandable 'how this is made' list under a part, so the 'expand the 6510' gesture survives.

step.test: Is this the preceding stage of the same recipe?
step.note: Stored three ways, all meaning "an operation in whose making I take part". process->process is the recipe chain. part->process and material->process point from the thing being made at an operation in its manufacture, and are what lets a viewer expand a part and see its manufacturing flow. The round-2 removal from material->process was made when `step` had no legal storage there at all; it was restored after round 3 established that storage, and material->process keeps DELETE for the redundant-intermediate case because that reading scored 95%. ASYMMETRY FLAGGED: the two pairs now treat an intermediate stage differently. Not measured either way since the change.
step.count_note: 404 process->process, plus part->process and material->process once those are classified.

consumes.test: Does it go in? Reagents, feedstock, consumables, and utilities.
consumes.note: Target is always a material. Utilities are materials, so `process -> Electricity at the factory wall` is `consumes`, and every facility target becomes unambiguously `at`. facility->material is the plant's own feedstock.
consumes.count_note: 628 of the 922 process->material edges came from the `inputs` field, which means they were recorded as inputs and are therefore `consumes` mechanically. See RELATIONS.md §8.

produces.note: `role` is required so that `Acid neutralisation with lime -> heavy-metal hydroxide sludge` does not read as a product. The canonical stored form of a making relationship; `made by` is derived from it.

uses.test: Is this capital equipment the operation needs? Also the one place a part or material may be the source: read it as 'making me involves this equipment', for the case where a machine is named with no process node in between.
uses.note: `tool->process` is here because those 20 edges are STORED BACKWARDS and get reversed into `process->tool`. `part->tool` and `material->tool` are legal but should be rare -- in each case first ask whether the target is really a process mis-typed as a tool. Carries connectivity (DECIDED 2026-10-04); see `connectivity.uses_note`.

at.note: NOT ownership. Ownership is `owned by` to an `org`. Once `org` is a kind, this relation needs no judgement at all -- which was the reason it was merged in the first place. `site->tool` and `facility->tool` are stored REVERSED: equipment standing inside a place is `at` that place, read from the equipment's side. `org->facility`/`org->site` are a subsidiary's site, stored reversed for the same reason.

owned by.arrow: none -- not part of the supply walk
owned by.note: Not connectivity-carrying. Commodore's vertical integration through MOS Technology is the central ownership story of this tree and it deserves a relation of its own rather than being bent into `at`. `org->org` is the subsidiary chain (a division owned by its parent company); the parent is the target.

about.test: Is this a note rather than a thing?
about.note: The only relation a note may participate in, in either direction. A note with any outgoing non-`about` edge is a mis-typed node or an index, and is an audit FAIL.

hub_rules.$comment: Relations fixed BY TARGET NODE, overriding the kind-pair table. These are the high-fan-in nodes whose relation is not in doubt, so no agent should spend a decision on them. relate.mjs checks these BEFORE the judgement questions. 8 utility deliveries: measured 241 edges point at the first five, plus the three water variants found during Wave 1 calibration.

facility.electricity.why: you consume electricity. Nothing else is possible.

hub_rules._fanin: Electricity 177, water 47, steam 6, gases 4, compressed air 2. By source kind: process 118, tool 59, material 26, facility 17, part 12, org 6, site 2, note 1. The 118 process edges and 59 tool edges are what this rule rescues from the judgement pass.
hub_rules._note: The concrete form of 'hubs have a central owner' (RELATIONS.md section 9, wave 3). The hub NODES are central; the edges INTO them are mechanical.

facility.water.industrial.why: ordinary industrial water is drawn in

facility.water.di-loop.why: the distribution loop delivers water that is drawn in

judgement_questions.$comment: Every kind-pair that needs a human decision, and the test that settles it. Kept HERE rather than in relate.mjs so the audit and the work lists read the same list. relate.mjs refuses to classify an edge that is in none of these and no relation's `stored` list -- that is what UNMAPPED means, and getting it to zero is the test that the schema is complete.
judgement_questions._delete_is_always_available: ADDED 2026-10-04 after Wave 1 calibration. BOTH agents independently reported that a test which cannot say 'this edge is wrong' forces known-bad edges into a residue bucket and produces a confident false label. Agent A: a test that cannot say this edge is wrong will generate confident false labels on exactly this class -- and named three it had to dump into 'made from'. So DELETE is a legal answer on every question below. An edge can be wrong without its kind-pair being unusual, and 441 of the 908 material->material edges cannot be confirmed from the parent's own description at all, so the parent text is not a reliable oracle either.
judgement_questions._index_parents_are_not_yours: ADDED 2026-10-04. 80 edges leave an index or grouping node (c64.bottoms-out, unlinked.catalogue, industry, c64.extras, metal, logistics.*, facility.foundries). Both agents hit these and had no valid answer, because no relation means anything from a node that exists only to hold others. DO NOT decide these: report them and move on. Wave 4.2/4.3 dissolves the index nodes and gives those edges real parents. See _index_parents below.

material->material.test: Would a spec sheet for the parent list the target as a component? Yes, or the parent is the SAME substance in a different shape -> `made of`. Reacted, reduced, alloyed, melted into a network or separated -> `made from`.
material->material.note: The largest and hardest. Ten worked borderline cases in RELATIONS.md 3.1, plus 5 + 9 in the `made of` / `made from` examples above. This is the pair the calibration gate measures.

process->material.test: Does it go in or come out? A named feedstock, reagent, catalyst, utility or consumable goes IN. The product, co-product, sludge or off-gas comes OUT. Read the verb in the process's `description` when unsure.
process->material.provenance_shortcut: 628 of the 922 came from the `inputs` prose field and are therefore `consumes`. NOT TRUSTED -- see verification_required. All 628 get an agent verdict first.

part->material.test: Could you point at it? A discrete slug, pellet, casing, wire or layer physically IN the part -> `contains`. A resin, solder, adhesive or plating dispersed through or coated onto it -> `made of`.

tool->material.test: Is it a consumable the machine eats (drill bits, coolant, grinding wheel), or a permanent fitting of the machine (a motor, a guard, a cabinet)? Consumable -> `uses` reversed. Fitting -> `contains`.

facility->material.test: Is it the plant's product (a gas supply plant produces nitrogen; a refinery produces fuel oil)? -> `produces`, reversed. Or is it a fixture of the plant (piping, a lining, a cable)? -> `at`, reversed.

part->process.decide: produces (reversed) | step | REFILE as part>material | kind bug (retype part->tool, then uses reversed) | DELETE
part->process.test: Three real questions, then delete. (1) Is the operation's output a DISTINCT COMPONENT that ends up inside me -- a separate object? A grading step whose output is a powder that goes into the capacitor; a metallising run whose output is a film that goes into me. -> `REFILE as part>material`, and record it. NOT this when the operation changes a FEATURE of me rather than adding a separate object: plating, chroming, HASL, enamelling, potting, blackening, etching, printing, PRESS FORMING. A layer on me is not a component of me. TWO EXCEPTIONS, both added in round 4: (a) if the output BECOMES the part's load-bearing element rather than an insert inside it -- a grown blank, a green sheet, an etched foil roll, a formed casing -- answer `REFILE` and record that the finishing step is unmodelled; (b) a SHARED material node (metal.solder, metal.copper) is never a component of me: if the material is the tree's canonical node for a substance rather than a part-specific one, it is not an insert. (2) DID I EXIST AS MYSELF BEFORE THIS OPERATION? No -- the operation brings me into being, and its output is me as finally sold -> `produces`, stored on the process. Exactly one per node. Yes -- it refines, finishes, coats, trims, grades or tests me -> `step`. The board exists before the HASL dip. The mask exists before photoetching. The transistor exists before die-attach. TIE-BREAK, and it is not optional: if I have other modelled stages, `produces` goes to the LAST one named in my own description, and every earlier stage is `step`. My own description decides what `me` means. Without this, a parent with six modelled stages answers 'no, I did not exist' six times and trips `produces_must_be_unique`. (3) Is the operation's output a LARGER OBJECT THAT MERELY CONTAINS ME -- a cable assembly containing the plug, a PSU containing a bolting regulator, pack-out closing a box of already-finished parts? -> `DELETE`. The containment is recorded on the larger node, so this edge is a duplicate of it. (4) Otherwise `DELETE`, including any child that is commentary rather than an operation: report it, because `about` only accepts a `note` target and kind changes are central.
part->process.never_default_to_produces: If nothing qualifies under clause 2's first limb, do NOT promote the last one. Report that nothing produces this node. Measured worse than first recorded: 8 of 27 sampled parents ended with no producer (round 2 recorded 4 of 20). That is a content gap worth surfacing, not a relation to invent.
part->process.note: ROUND 3: known-hard rows 8/9 = 89%, so the finishing clause works. FRESH rows 13/18 = 72%, and all six disagreements trace to three causes, two of them structural: (a) THREE of six were the assembly hole -- an operation whose output is a LARGER object containing the parent, which no clause covered; now clause 3. Both agents named it independently, and agent A said it 'arguably wants a contains-reversed relation, which the answer list does not offer'. (b) ONE was a kind bug: c64.mains.switch.contacts.copper-silver is named 'Copper and silver ores' and typed `part`. (c) TWO were clause 2 contradicting ITSELF: as written ('the operation's OUTPUT is a materially different precursor that becomes me') the output is the precursor, which selects an EARLY operation, while its own gloss ('the one operation that gets produces') requires the output to be me, which selects the LAST. Opposite answers wherever the output is an intermediate. Clause 2 is now keyed on 'did I exist as myself before this operation', which has no such ambiguity. Only one disagreement (process-node granularity: a node bundling a winding vs one bundling the whole capacitor) looks irreducible.

round4.agents_disagreed: Agent A: the clause-2 contradiction is dead, it "worked on every row". Agent B: it still contradicts itself. B was right.
round4.why_A_was_wrong: A tested on single-chain parents, where the question ("did I exist before") and the gloss ("output is me as finally sold") cannot diverge. B noticed they part company whenever the modelled child is an EARLY stage.
round4.verified_exposure: 35 part nodes carry two or more modelled process stages, covering 149 of the 300 edges. mb.pcb has 10 operations, mb.cpu 9, mb.pla 8, mb.roms 8, mb.ram 8. A literal reading claims `produces` on every child: 114 spurious produces_must_be_unique failures.
fixes: clause 2 gained an explicit tie-break: `produces` goes to the LAST stage named in the parent description, earlier stages are `step`. One sentence, and it settles the y1 / mlcc / magnet-wire / alu-capacitor family.
the clause-1 examples now describe the OUTPUT rather than the operation, so the mica-metallisation case (a run that dices the stack into capacitors) is no longer captured by them.
added `kind bug (retype part->tool, then uses reversed)` so equipment typed `part` has somewhere to go.
round4.coverage_caveat: Agent B: every parent in the round-4 sample was a single-chain family. The genuinely hard multi-stage parents that dominated rounds 2 and 3 are absent from it, so round-4 agreement is optimistic for the 149-edge multi-stage residue even after the fix.
round4.irreducible: Process-node granularity. mb.passives.caps.tantalum.dielectric and mb.passives.caps.mica.metallisation are the same shape of physics decided differently because of how the author drew the node. Third appearance across rounds; not fixable by wording.
round4.score: UNMEASURED after these fixes. Wave 2 proceeds regardless, per instruction. part->process is calibrated-with-caveats and the multi-stage residue (149 edges) is the least-tested part of the migration.

material->process.test: THREE questions, in this order. (1) Does the operation TAKE THE MATERIAL IN, so that the edge is stored the wrong way round? A solar salt pond consumes brine and yields halite; a die-caster consumes the ingot; a loom re-forms E-glass strand into cloth. -> `REVERSE to consumes`. (2) Is this the one operation whose output is the material as it is finally sold -- a materially different precursor becoming me? -> `produces`, stored on the process. Exactly one per node. (3) Otherwise `DELETE`: an intermediate stage of my own making is already implied by the `step` chain between the processes, so a product-to-intermediate-step edge is a duplicate of that chain, and storing it gives two records that will drift.
material->process.note: ROUND 2: agreement rose 40% -> 95% (19/20), so the `REVERSE to consumes` clause is doing its job. `step` was REMOVED from this list: agent B pointed out that `step` is stored only as process->process, so a material->process edge answered `step` had no legal storage direction at all. That was my error, not a judgement problem -- intermediate stages are `DELETE` here because the step chain already carries them.

facility->part.test: Is it a fixture of the place (an access floor panel in a cleanroom)? -> `at`, reversed. Or does the operation MAKE it (a logistics office produces a bill of lading)? -> `produces`, reversed.

facility->tool.test: Equipment standing inside a plant. Always `at`, reversed.
facility->tool.note: NEW, same run. Mechanical once recognised.

part->tool.test: Is the target a machine or an operation? `Injection moulding press and tool`, `Firing in a continuous belt kiln`, `Hot platen press and the lamination cycle` are OPERATIONS wearing `kind: tool` -- retype, then `made by`. `Case tooling: H13 family mould`, `The mask writer`, `Vacuum deposition bell` are genuine EQUIPMENT -> `uses`.
part->tool.note: NEW, same run. Half of these are kind bugs.

material->tool.decide: uses | at | kind bug (retype tool->process) | DELETE
material->tool.test: Same shape as part->tool, plus one clause agent A found: is the machine the utility plant's OWN FIXTURE? `Industrial steam plant -> Industrial turbo-alternator` is a generator belonging to the steam plant, not a tool the steam is made with -> `at`. This whole class is a consequence of the Wave 0 utility retypes, so it will grow if more are retyped.

tool->process.decide: REVERSE to uses | reassign to contains | DELETE
tool->process.test: Does the operation happen INSIDE the machine (`The single-deck electrolysis cell -> Strip the cathodes`)? -> reverse to `uses`. Is the machine made OF something the process makes (`saw blade -> Industrial diamond from graphite`)? -> `contains`. Or is it already stored the other way round? -> DELETE.
tool->process.note: NEW, same run. Split is in `reversals`.

facility->process.test: An operation carried out inside a plant. Always `at`, reversed -- unless the plant IS the operation, in which case the node should be `process`, not `facility`.

site>material.test: Does the site DRAW IT IN (a metallisation bay draws argon and power; an intake draws river water) -> `consumes` reversed. Does it MAKE IT (a producer site makes trichloroethene) -> `produces` reversed. Is the site itself BUILT OF it (a cryogenic storage tank is built of stainless and aluminium) -> `made of` reversed.

site>part.test: Is the part a fixture OF the site (an access floor panel under a raised floor)? -> `contains` reversed, if the site can meaningfully contain things. Or is it merely co-located? -> `at`.
site>part.note: NEW. Only 2 edges, and the distinction is thin at this size.

material>part.test: Same shape as the original 18, plus one new arrival: `Electricity at the factory wall -> Busbar trunking and cable`. Electricity is not MADE OF busbar, it is DELIVERED THROUGH it. Delete it, or record it as delivery infrastructure rather than composition.
material>part.note: Most of these are already decided in data/_relation_fixes.json. This question exists for the residue plus anything the retypes moved.

reversals.$comment: Edges stored in the wrong direction. Deliberately NOT part of the mechanical kind-pair pass: each class needs a human decision, which is what docs/assessment.md §1 caught and what the first draft of RELATIONS.md got wrong.

tool->process.detail: The 4 are * -> Industrial diamond from graphite (saw blade, grinding wheel, scriber and dicing saw). Arrow direction is right, relation is wrong: the tools contain diamond, they do not use the process that makes it. The kind bug is `Alkaline scrubber packing -> Polypropylene`, where Polypropylene is typed `process`.

material->part.detail: NONE of these reverse mechanically. 7 already have the opposite edge stored as `from`, so reversing would make a third copy. Of the rest, `High-purity silicon feedstock -> quartz clock crystal` is simply wrong (silicon and quartz are unrelated), `Oxygen supply -> Acetylene cylinder` is wrong (a cylinder is steel), `Copper -> Blister copper anode` duplicates `cathode -> anode`, and four separate wire nodes all point at `Enamelled magnet wire` -- the signature of a name-index accident on the word 'wire'.

calibration_findings.$comment: What Wave 1 measured, and what was changed as a result. Kept so a later session does not re-derive it or undo it.
calibration_findings.result: 76 edges, two agents blind. Overall agreement 88.2%. GATE 1 PASSED: material->material 15/16 = 93.8%, threshold 85%.

failed_and_rewritten.material->process: 2/5 (40%) on 301 edges. ALL THREE disagreements were one thing: the process consumes the material and the edge is stored backwards. Neither agent had an answer for it. REWRITTEN: 'does the operation take the material in' is now the FIRST question, with `REVERSE to consumes` as an answer.
failed_and_rewritten.part->process: 3/5 (60%) on 300 edges. Agent A: the 'last modelled step yields the part' rule was doing real work and was not written down. Agent B found a missing clause: is the process making something that goes INTO the part? REWRITTEN with a four-step ordered test including `REFILE as part>material`.

changes_made: DELETE is now a legal answer on EVERY judgement question. Both agents demanded it independently.
`part->process` gained `REFILE as part>material` and a written ordering rule.
`material->tool` gained `at` for the plant's own fixture.
Index/grouping node parents are declared NOT the agent's to decide. 80 edges; report only.
_judgement_overrides_mechanical: the judgement question is authoritative wherever one exists.
The `metal.copper -> metal.copper.wire` worked example is WITHDRAWN as circular; the edge becomes DELETE.
3 more utility deliveries retyped facility -> material (facility.water.industrial, .ultrapure, .di-loop), found by chasing agent B's argon report.

measurements_worth_keeping.441 of 908: material->material edges cannot be confirmed from the parent's own description, including legitimate ones like E-glass fibre -> Borax. The parent text is NOT a reliable oracle; agents must read both ends.
measurements_worth_keeping.80 edges: leave an index or grouping node. Centrally handled in Wave 4.
measurements_worth_keeping.300 edges / 27 parents: part->process parents with three or more process steps, which is why the ordering rule had to be written.
measurements_worth_keeping.19 edges: material->tool, a direct consequence of the Wave 0 utility retypes.

round2.result: 40 edges, the two rewritten questions only. Overall 31/40 = 77.5%.
round2.material_to_process: 2/5 -> 19/20 = 95%. The REVERSE to consumes clause works. `step` removed from the answer list after agent B showed it has no legal storage direction for this kind-pair.
round2.part_to_process: 3/5 -> 12/20 = 60%. Unchanged, but the residual is now ONE pattern: 6 of 9 disagreements were plating, chroming, HASL, enamelling and pad plating on the very object the parent names. Both agents gave the same clause-1 fix independently. A third clause was added: a finishing operation whose output is the same object is `step`, never `produces`.
round2.the_trap_both_agents_named: "Last MODELLED operation" degenerates to "only modelled operation". Agent A: 11 of 20 parents had exactly one process child. Agent B used "only modelled op, therefore last" to justify `produces` on all six plating rows. Hence never_default_to_produces: if nothing qualifies, report it rather than promoting the last one.
round2.residual_uncertainty: `step` was 35% of all answers across both rounds. It is the catch-all, and the catch-all is where a test's real uncertainty lives. Watch it in Wave 3.
round2.untested: `about` was offered on part->process and used 0/20 times in either round. It is still unverified.

round3.known_hard: 8/9 = 89%. The finishing clause works. Both agents resolved seven plating rows by matching the carve-out, which is the clause doing its job rather than the agent reasoning.

causes.assembly_hole: THREE of six disagreements. An operation whose output is a LARGER object containing the parent: cable assembly containing the plug, PSU containing a bolting regulator, pack-out closing a box of already-finished parts. No clause covered it. Now clause 3, answered DELETE, because the containment is already recorded on the larger node. Both agents named it independently.
causes.clause_2_self_contradiction: TWO of six. As written it selected an EARLY operation (output is the precursor); its own gloss selected the LAST (output is me). Re-keyed on "did I exist as myself before this operation", which is unambiguous.
causes.kind_bug: ONE. c64.mains.switch.contacts.copper-silver is named "Copper and silver ores" and typed `part`. Refining consumes ores.
causes.irreducible: ONE. Process-node granularity: a node bundling only the winding and a node bundling the whole capacitor get different answers from identical physics. The discriminator is how the author drew the node, not what happens in the factory.

round3.content_gaps: 8 of 27 sampled parents end with no producer, worse than the 4 of 20 recorded after round 2. The tree under-models the operation that brings many parts into being.
round3.index_parents_leaked: Agent A: c64.packaging and c64.mains are both index nodes and both appeared in the 300-edge part->process set, which contradicts the rule that index parents are centrally handled. The set needs filtering by _index_parents.
round3.pattern_across_three_rounds: Every round's deepest finding was STRUCTURAL, not editorial: four missing questions in round 1, a storage bug in round 2, two more storage bugs plus a self-contradictory clause in round 3. Agreement percentages hid all of them. 60% reads like unclear wording; it was twice an answer with nowhere to go.

round4.known_hard: n/a -- round 4 was fresh-parents only, by design.
round4.fresh: 22 edges, every parent unseen in rounds 2 and 3. Agent A: 12 high / 8 medium / 2 low confidence; answers 10 produces, 6 step, 5 REFILE, 1 DELETE.
round4.what_is_fixed: ALL 22 edges took a legal, storable answer. The storage defect that killed rounds 2 and 3 is gone. Clause 2 self-contradiction is gone -- "did I exist as myself before" worked on every row and never needed its parenthetical qualifier.
round4.what_is_not: Clause 1 pre-empts clause 2 on precursor-becomes-load-bearing-element: mica counter-electrode, tantalum dielectric, green sheets, etched foil roll. 4 of 22 fresh rows = 18%, so roughly 50 of the 300 edges. Agent A also found clause 1 contradicting itself via the word "forming" (in the carve-out list, but anodic formation is literally forming), and no shared-material carve-out, which is what let mainboard soldering reach clause 1 at all.
round4.agent_A_verdict: "No -- but it is close, and the remaining fault is one sentence wide, not structural." Predicted agreement without the fixes: 75-80%. With its two edits plus the shared-material carve-out: apply to 300 edges unchanged.
fixes_applied: clause 1 exception (a): output BECOMES the load-bearing element -> REFILE, and record the unmodelled finishing step
clause 1 exception (b): a SHARED material node is never a component of me
_index_parents += mb.passives.caps (a grouping node that was leaking into agent sets)
mb.solder.wave.preheat retyped part -> tool (an oven, so its edge can store as tool->process)
round4.score_after_fixes: UNMEASURED. The user directed that Wave 2 proceed regardless, and three of the four causes are addressed. Treat part->process as calibrated-with-caveats and watch `step` share in Wave 3.
round4.content_gap_persists: 6 of 22 fresh parents (27%) end with no producer, consistent with round 3's 8/27. Four have only a finishing operation modelled. This is a tree content gap, not a relation problem.

edge_attributes.$comment: Cheap to add during the relabel and expensive to add later, because they have to be attached to edges that have already been rewritten.

basis.note: This is a historical reconstruction. Some edges are documented for 1982, others inferred from generic industrial practice, and the viewer should be able to say which.

role.note: Distinguishes the wanted output from a by-product or a pollutant.

source.note: Optional, per edge rather than per node.

audit_rules.$comment: Checks for scripts/audit.mjs, all driven from this file so the prose cannot drift from the gate. All are tree-wide, so per HANDOFF §6 they must be run centrally after any fan-out, not only per fragment. Severity is stated explicitly; nothing is an implicit FAIL.
audit_rules.kind_pair_not_in_schema: FAIL. (source kind, target kind) is not in the relation's `stored` list.
audit_rules.consumes_target_is_part: FAIL. Explicitly forbidden by narrow_kinds. No edge needs it.
audit_rules.note_with_outgoing_non_about_edge: FAIL. A note with supply edges is a mis-typed node or an index node.
audit_rules.made_from_paralleling_a_process_route: WARN with agreement check. Redundancy is sanctioned; disagreement is not. FAIL only if the shortcut contradicts the route.
audit_rules.duplicate_inverse_encoding: FAIL. `made by` is derived, so it cannot be stored; this catches a hand edit that reintroduces it.
audit_rules.directed_upstream_reachability: FAIL if any node in data/ is unreachable from the root by the connectivity rule above.
audit_rules.ingredient_string_names_a_product_not_a_: WARN. Measured: 63 of 155 curated rows in _ingredients.json give a string absent from the target node's name -- `"iron ore"` -> Hematite, `"copper ore"` -> the Copper product index, `"sodium dichromate"` -> a process. Nine rows point at a process, three at a facility. See RELATIONS.md 7.3.
audit_rules.produces_must_be_unique: FAIL. Two operations both claiming `produces` for the same node means the tie-break was not applied. Agent B justified six plating edges as "only modelled operation, therefore last" -- exactly the failure this rule exists to catch.
audit_rules.every_entity_should_have_a_producer: WARN. A part or material with process steps but no operation qualifying under part->process clause 2 means its real producer is unmodelled. 4 of 20 sampled parents were in this state. A content gap to surface, not a relation to invent -- see judgement_questions.part->process.never_default_to_produces.
audit_rules.answer_must_be_storable: FAIL. An edge assigned an answer whose relation cannot store that kind-pair is not a classification, it is a shrug. This is the check that would have caught `step` and `about` on part->process in round 3, and `step` on material->process in round 2. Mechanically checkable: every answer in a judgement question's `decide` list must name a relation whose `stored` list accepts the kind-pair. Run it in `relate.mjs plan`.

open_questions.$comment: All four of RELATIONS.md §11 are now DECIDED. Kept as a record so the reasoning is not lost, and so a later session can see what was settled and on what grounds.
open_questions.produces_target_may_be_part: DECIDED: `produces -> part` allowed (moulding yields the case). `consumes -> part` NOT allowed and now explicitly so in `narrow_kinds` -- a process takes in substances, not discrete objects, and no edge in the tree needs it.
open_questions.uses_carries_connectivity: DECIDED: YES, downward from a reached process. Measured cost zero today (the 195 tool nodes are already downward-reachable via `children`). Revisitable, per the user's note.
open_questions.made_from_allowed_at_all: DECIDED: KEEP, as a deliberate redundancy and as a visual convenience. The parallel-route audit drops from FAIL to WARN-with-agreement-check.
open_questions.inputs_provenance_trust: DECIDED: DO NOT TRUST. All 628 process->material edges derived from `inputs` get verified by parallel agents before they are written. See RELATIONS.md §9 wave 2.

verification_required.$comment: Edges that must be checked by a human or an agent before being written. Recorded so no wave skips them.

inputs_derived_consumes.why: `from` is derived from the `inputs` prose field, so these were recorded as requirements. That is good evidence for `consumes`, but 63 of 155 curated rows in _ingredients.json name a product or a process rather than a substance, so the target can be wrong.
inputs_derived_consumes.gate: verified by parallel agents, sliced; no edge is written unverified

gold_set_calibration.why: The `made of` / `made from` test covers 898 edges. Two agents label the same 80 blind; if agent-agent agreement is below 85% the test wording is wrong, not the agents.

out_of_scope.supplier_and_transport_flow: Which company shipped which part from where to whom. Expressible only indirectly today. Named here so that agents do not bend `at` to carry it.

wave2_ingredient_audit.summary: 63 suspect rows audited by hand. RIGHT 28, WRONG TARGET 20, NOT AN INGREDIENT 4, UNSURE 11. Only 44% of the rows that failed the name test are actually right.
wave2_ingredient_audit.all_20_replacements_verified: Every proposed replacement id already exists in the tree and is a material (49 is a part). No cycles or self-loops introduced. Highest value: si.emc is a material node titled "Silica-filled epoxy moulding compound" with si.emc.silica as a child, and THREE rows were pointing at the generic epoxy PROCESS while the exact answer sat in 10-silicon.json. facility.water's own description instructs consumers to point at facility.water.ultrapure.
wave2_ingredient_audit.self_loop_found: "pine stumps" -> chem.rosin, and chem.rosin's own inputs array contains "pine stumps", so the row resolved to itself.
wave2_ingredient_audit.MY_FRAMING_WAS_WRONG: I wrote that nine rows point at a process, three at a facility, one at a tool, and that "those cannot be ingredients of anything under the new relation set". Only ONE of the four NOT AN INGREDIENT verdicts points at a process. Of the nine process-target rows, eight are perfectly good ingredient STRINGS with a process as the TARGET -- wrong target, not a non-ingredient. I also cited `boric acid -> chem.glass-fiber.borax.acid` as an example of a CORRECT name match; that node is a process ("Boric acid from colemanite"), so my own worked example was invalid.
wave2_ingredient_audit.the_real_pattern: Table-wide there are 26 process-target rows and 20 of them sit in 70-petrochem.json -- and they are ONE bug, not twenty. That file's branch-head nodes are production ROUTES, not substances: chem.ethylene = "Ethylene: steam cracking...", chem.styrene = "Styrene: benzene plus ethylene...", chem.abs = "ABS resin plant...", chem.crude = "Crude oil: finding it, drilling it...". The table maps a material name onto the plant that makes it. Affected: methanol, ethylene, propylene, butadiene, styrene, acrylonitrile, abs resin, pvc, polyester, polyethylene, polycarbonate, silicone, photoresist, crude oil, epoxy.
wave2_ingredient_audit.the_name_test_is_not_a_safety_filter: The 63 rows that failed "the string is in the name" test are the VISIBLE half. 17 of the 26 process-target rows are among the 90 that PASSED it (crude oil, methanol, ethylene, styrene, PVC, polyester, photoresist). Passing the name test bought nothing.
wave2_ingredient_audit.two_more_defects: Two rows point at ids that do not exist (nylon, nylon 6 6) -- dangling references in a table nothing validates. And 28 target ids are shared by more than one string, up to six for metal.rare-earths.bastnasite, so the table is a many-to-one funnel: a fix that helps one row usually breaks a synonym for another. Retargeting `soda silica` and `silica filler` off metal.silica-sand was only safe because their siblings (`silica sand`, `quartz sand`) are separate rows pointing at the same node.
wave2_ingredient_audit.the_blocking_problem_is_the_tree: Eight UNSURE rows are not unreadable nodes -- they are substances the tree has no node for: Na2Cr2O7, Al(OH)3, ZnCl2, a Co-Ni catalyst, BeCu, a generic nickel ore, a generic `paper`, PVC resin, TiCl4, 2-ethylhexanol. Three are gaps the tree contradicts itself on: chem.pvc is a process with no resin child at all, five separate paper nodes exist with nothing above them, and nickel has both a laterite and a Sudbury sulphide branch.
wave2_ingredient_audit.recommended_disposition: Retarget the 20 verified rows. Delete the 4 NOT AN INGREDIENT rows. Treat the remaining 131 rows as UNAUDITED rather than correct. The name test is not evidence of safety and must not be used as one.

wave2_process_edges.verdict_rate: Slices 1-3: 92%, 80%, 81% precision on the inputs-derived process->material edges. 59 rejections out of 393 edges reviewed.
wave2_process_edges.the_errors_are_authored_not_matched: Slice 1 traced provenance: 153 of 158 edges came from an author typing an EXACT node id. Bare-noun strings that the matcher resolved by name are only 11% of the population. So these are author judgement errors, not string-match noise. Decision D -- do not trust the provenance -- was right, and for a stronger reason than first stated: the provenance is not weak evidence about a good field, it is good evidence about a wrong field.
wave2_process_edges.precision_varies_by_fragment: metals is well curated (7 errors in 96 edges); the logic fragment is where the damage is. data/32-passives-b.json (connector-jacks) is the least reliable subtree in the tree -- 4 wrong in 42, including two cases of a completely unrelated substance.

systemic_magnets.metal_silica: 51 inbound edges tree-wide. It is the 9N crystal-pull charge. Slices 2 and 3 independently found EVERY one of its edges in their slices wrong for fab and packaging steps -- the author assigned it to anything whose text mentioned silica or silicon. Needs a central decision, not 51 agent decisions.
systemic_magnets.chem_petroleum: A dead-end leaf with ZERO children, used as a universal petrochemical stamp. Every petroleum edge is a two-or-three-step-downstream shortcut that should attach to the cracker or read as `made from`, not `consumes`.
systemic_magnets.product_index_nodes: metal.copper, metal.nickel, metal.tin, metal.gold are self-referential product indexes, already flagged in kinds.content_defects_found. Edges resolving through them will not survive a strict audit.

schema_gaps_found.no_wafer_material_node: si.wafer is kind part, so "the wafer being processed" is not a legal `consumes` target. Wafer-level process steps are correct in substance and have nowhere to point. Needs a wafer material node.
schema_gaps_found.no_home_for_durable_tooling: `uses` targets tools only, so metal.aluminum.extrusion -> metal.die-steel (a die is capital equipment, not consumed) has no legal relation. Three edges.
schema_gaps_found.inputs_dead_ends: About 20% of all `inputs` entries resolve to nothing and produce NO edge; the substance is absent from the tree and nothing reports it. Worst: phosphine 13x, arsine 8x -- both ALREADY recorded in TODO.md section 8 as the worst cases of a normalisation bug that was never fixed. Concentrated in 90-peripherals (220), 40-chassis (160), 80-industry (133).

content_bugs: metal.hall-heroult.dross has inputs ["metal.alumina","metal.carbon.anode"] -- both are the POT's feed. Dross is a waste stream with no node at all.
metal.salt-brine landed on a gold cyanide bath where a sodium-cyanide node already exists as a child of that very node.
wave2_process_edges.ordering_rule: Deleting a wrong edge without adding the right one leaves a hole. sphalerite -> zinc electroplating is wrong, but the tree does NOT draw metal.zinc as an input to that finishing step either, so removing the edge orphans the chain. Fix additions and deletions together, per node.
wave2_process_edges.brief_defect_found: Both slice 2 and slice 3 independently reported that the `note` field settles ingredients MORE reliably than `description`, and my brief only pointed them at `description`. Wave 3 briefs must read both.

wave2.status: COMPLETE. Six slice agents reviewed the 642 inputs-derived process->material edges; a seventh agent reviewed the 68 remaining inbound edges to the two magnets. 710 edges reviewed in total. Nothing has been applied to the tree.
wave2.verdict: 552 kept as `consumes`, 158 rejected (22.3%). Rejection confidence: 80 high, 77 medium, 1 low. Precision by slice: 92%, 80%, 81%, 92%, 88%, 79% -- the metals fragments are well curated, the logic and passives fragments are not.
wave2.THE_STRUCTURAL_FINDING: 41% of the rejections -- 65 of 158 -- were not judgement calls at all. They were edges that were never `consumes`-capable in the first place, because `consumes` is stored process/tool/facility -> material and their parents were a `material` (38), a `part` (25), a `note` (1) or unlocatable (1). A material row with an `inputs` array gets those inputs stamped onto it regardless of whether an operation is involved. The other 93 rejections ARE real judgement calls on schema-legal parents, and each needs an individual disposition.
wave2.why_the_magnets_looked_like_magnets: This answers the question six agents each answered from a biased slice. `metal.silica`: 51 of 51 rejected, across both waves, zero survivors. `chem.petroleum`: 47 of 52 rejected, 5 kept -- and all 5 survivors are a `process` or a `tool`, i.e. exactly the schema-legal shapes. Zero materials and zero parts survived on either magnet. The pattern is not chemistry. An edge is wrong on these two nodes because nothing about the parent says an operation happened.

per_slice_precision.2 logic + petrochem + industry: 80% (25 of 122 wrong) -- mb.logic.bipolar.litho.strip is the worst single parent, 4 of its 8 edges point at petrochemical feedstocks that have no role in a resist strip
per_slice_precision.4 metals-b + metals-c + board: 92% (7 of 92) -- cleanest slice; no magnet rows at all

wave2.the_errors_are_authored_not_matched: Slice 1 traced provenance: 153 of 158 edges came from an author typing an EXACT node id. Bare-noun strings resolved by name are only 11% of the population. `mb.rf-modulator.hybrid-module.assembly` has inputs ["metal.silica"] -- an exact id, simply wrong. Decision D was right, and for a stronger reason than first stated: the provenance is not weak evidence about a good field, it is good evidence about a wrong field. No string-form test can detect these.
wave2.the_name_test_is_not_a_safety_filter: For the lookup table: the 63 rows that failed the "string is in the name" test are the VISIBLE half. 17 of the 26 process-target rows are among the 90 that PASSED it. Passing bought nothing. Disposition: retarget the 20 verified, delete the 4 NOT AN INGREDIENT, treat the remaining 131 as UNAUDITED rather than correct.
wave2.ordering_rule_for_applying: A rejection is not automatically a deletion. 25 of the 68 magnet parents had the magnet as their SOLE input and 18 of those are genuine holes -- `metal.steel.eaf` would have no metal charge at all, `metal.solder.cleaning` would be left with only the residue it removes, and the petrochemical trunk loses its last crude link because `chem.refining.atmospheric-distillation` has inputs: []. Apply additions and deletions together, per node, or the tree gets worse in a new place.
wave2.brief_defects_found: FOUR agents independently reported that `note` settles ingredients more reliably than `description`, and my brief only pointed them at `description`. Where a note flagged tension, the note won every time. PowerShell eats `$` in inline `node -e` scripts and produces dozens of phantom parse errors; put validation in a .js file. And every parent in the round-4 calibration sample was a single-chain family, so round-4 agreement is optimistic for the 149-edge multi-stage residue.

no home for durable tooling -- `uses` targets tools only, so metal.aluminum.extrusion -> metal.die-steel (a die is capital equipment, not consumed) has no relation at all
no relation for "consumed as ambience or forming gas" -- bipolar.process.sinter -> facility.nitrogen, and forming gases generally

about 20% of all `inputs` entries resolve to nothing and produce NO edge; the substance is absent from the tree and nothing reports it. Worst: phosphine 13x, arsine 8x, both ALREADY recorded in TODO.md section 8 as an unfixed normalisation bug
content_bugs_found: metal.hall-heroult.dross has inputs ["metal.alumina","metal.carbon.anode"] -- both are the POT's feed. Dross is a waste stream with no node at all.
metal.salt-brine landed on a gold cyanide bath where a sodium-cyanide node already exists as a child of that very node.
chem.styrene.benzene is NAMED "Benzene". Polymerisation of styrene points at it.
mb.passives.caps.mlcc.print-electrodes -> metal.nickel, but the node's own description and note say the 1982 paste was palladium-silver; nickel is dated to 1993. There is a metal.palladium node.

wave2.known_content_gap: 27% of sampled parents in rounds 3 and 4 end with no producer. The tree under-models the operation that brings many parts into being. This is not a relation problem and Wave 2 confirms it is not an ingredient problem either.
